sources.entry: KyttoMCP - Manage MCP servers across Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Codex in one matrix, with health checks, a tool safety scan and local config backups.

summary.one_liner: KyttoMCP is a free, open-source desktop app (macOS and Windows) that gives one matrix view and editor for MCP server configurations across Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Codex.
summary.what_it_does: Kytto reads the local MCP config files of five built-in clients and shows every server against every client in one matrix, where servers can be toggled, edited, or removed per client, each written in that client's own format. MCP Doctor runs an on-demand MCP handshake and reports tools, prompts, resources and stderr, flagging issues such as missing environment values, relative paths and unpinned package versions. A Tool Safety Scanner checks tool names, descriptions and schemas for hidden characters, instruction-like wording and duplicate tool names, and Contract Guard tracks tool definitions between health checks to report added, removed or changed tools. It also estimates tool-schema footprint, warns near VS Code's 128-tool limit, saves and applies profiles, masks and rotates secrets, and backs up every write so earlier configurations can be restored. An optional Gateway mode routes supported stdio servers through a local route with metadata-only activity logs.
use_cases: manage MCP servers across multiple AI clients
toggle MCP servers on or off per client
diagnose why an MCP server fails to start
scan MCP tool descriptions for prompt injection
switch between saved MCP server setups
back up and restore MCP client config files
how_to_run: Download Beta 1.0.9 from kytto.jakubhecht.sk or GitHub Releases (v1.0.9 for macOS, v1.0.9-windows for Windows)
macOS: open the DMG and drag KyttoMCP into Applications; Control-click and choose Open to bypass the unidentified developer warning
Windows: run the setup file; choose More info then Run anyway if SmartScreen appears
Build from source on macOS: cd KyttoMCP/macos && scripts/make-dmg.sh (Xcode 16+)
Run source tests: cd KyttoMCP/macos/KyttoCore && swift test, or cd KyttoMCP/windows && dotnet test
notable: Single matrix view of every MCP server against Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Codex
Tool Safety Scanner and Contract Guard flag prompt-injection-style wording, hidden characters and changed tool definitions
Every config write checks for outside changes, makes a timestamped backup and writes atomically
Custom read-only JSON, JSONC and TOML sources can be attached without being rewritten
Metadata-only Gateway mode with live activity log; payload capture is off
caveats: Installers are unsigned (no paid Apple or Windows certificate), so Gatekeeper and SmartScreen show warnings
Beta software; the README asks for honest criticism rather than praise
Safety scan is advisory only; a clean scan does not mean a server is trustworthy
Supports only the five listed clients for writes; custom sources are read-only
